passage:
"Uday, when Chacha comes tomorrow, tell him about your firm," Papa said, folding the newspaper. "Big name, no? I already told everyone."
Uday put his fork down. "Papa, I need to tell you something about the internship."
"Say."
"I'm not on the payroll. I'm an intern. Mostly I help with data entry and reports. It's not a salary job. I didn't correct you because you were so happy."
Papa was quiet for a while. "I told them because I was proud."
"I know. I'm proud too. I'm learning spreadsheets and how meetings work. And I'm applying for junior roles next month."
Papa nodded slowly. "Then tomorrow I will say: my son is learning at a big firm."
"That's true," said Uday.

qa.q: What did Papa ask Uday to tell Chacha about?
qa.a: Papa asked Uday to tell Chacha about his firm.

qa.q: Why had Uday not corrected Papa earlier?
qa.a: He did not want to spoil Papa's happiness, and he felt a guilty gap between what Papa told others and his own experience.

qa.q: What could Uday do next to keep Papa comfortable with the truth?
qa.a: He can share what he is learning and his plan to apply for junior roles, and keep Papa updated so pride can rest on facts.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt hearing the truth?
qa.a: Papa was quiet for a while, so he may have felt surprised or a little embarrassed. His offer to say "learning at a big firm" shows he still takes pride in Uday.

grounding: A parent proudly tells relatives about the big firm while the intern feels a guilty gap; he tells the truth gently and shares his plan.
